readingInstruction: Read Luke 24:1-53. The empty tomb, the road to Emmaus, the appearance to the disciples, and the ascension. This is the climax of the Gospel and the key to reading the whole Bible.
settingTheScene: On the first day of the week, at early dawn, the women come to the tomb with spices. The disciples are scattered and afraid. Luke’s last chapter takes place in a single day: the morning at the tomb, the afternoon on the road to Emmaus, and the evening in Jerusalem. It ends with the ascension, and leads straight into the book of Acts.
observation: “Why do you seek the living among the dead? He is not here, but has risen” (24:5-6).
“But we had hoped that he was the one to redeem Israel” (24:21).
“O foolish ones, and slow of heart to believe all that the prophets have spoken!” (24:25).
“And beginning with Moses and all the Prophets, he interpreted to them in all the Scriptures the things concerning himself” (24:27).
“Did not our hearts burn within us while he talked to us on the road, while he opened to us the Scriptures?” (24:32).
“See my hands and my feet, that it is I myself. Touch me, and see” (24:39).

“Thus it is written, that the Christ should suffer and on the third day rise from the dead, and that repentance for the forgiveness of sins should be proclaimed in his name to all nations” (24:46-47).
“And they worshiped him and returned to Jerusalem with great joy” (24:52).
interpretation:
The women find the stone rolled away and the tomb empty. Two men in dazzling clothes say, “Why do you seek the living among the dead? He is not here, but has risen.” They remind the women of what Jesus said in Galilee. The women tell the apostles, but the words seem to them an idle tale, and they do not believe. Peter runs to the tomb, sees the linen cloths, and goes home marveling.

That afternoon, two disciples walk to Emmaus, discussing the events. A stranger joins them, and they do not recognize him. He asks what they are talking about, and they stand still, looking sad. “We had hoped that he was the one to redeem Israel.” Their hope was crushed. The stranger replies, “O foolish ones, and slow of heart to believe all that the prophets have spoken! Was it not necessary that the Christ should suffer these things and enter into his glory?” And “beginning with Moses and all the Prophets, he interpreted to them in all the Scriptures the things concerning himself.”

This is the key to reading the whole Bible. All of Scripture, from Moses to the Prophets, points to Christ: his sufferings and his glory. The Old Testament is not a collection of unrelated stories. It is a single story that leads to him. This is the reason the Old Testament is read with the cross in view. At supper, in the breaking of the bread, their eyes were opened and they recognized him, and he vanished. “Did not our hearts burn within us while he talked to us on the road, while he opened to us the Scriptures?” They returned to Jerusalem the same hour.

While they are telling the others, Jesus himself stands among them and says, “Peace to you!” They think he is a ghost, and he shows them his hands and feet and eats a piece of broiled fish. The resurrection was bodily. Then he opens their minds to understand the Scriptures and says that everything written about him in the Law, the Prophets, and the Psalms must be fulfilled. The Christ suffers and rises, and repentance and forgiveness of sins are to be proclaimed in his name to all nations, beginning from Jerusalem. “You are witnesses of these things.” He promises the gift of the Holy Spirit, “the promise of my Father.”

He leads them out to Bethany, lifts up his hands, blesses them, and is carried up into heaven. They worship him and return to Jerusalem with great joy, continually in the temple blessing God. The Gospel that began in the temple with a priest who was struck silent ends in the temple with a people full of praise.
connection: Isaiah 53 and Psalm 22 are among the passages about the suffering and glory of the Christ. Genesis 3:15, Deuteronomy 18:15, 2 Samuel 7, and Psalm 110 are all part of the testimony. Acts 1:1-11 continues the story. 1 Corinthians 15:3-8 lists the appearances of the risen Christ. John 20:19-29 gives the parallel appearances. 2 Timothy 3:15 says the Scriptures are able to make you wise for salvation through faith in Christ Jesus. Hebrews 1:1-2 says God has spoken by his Son.
application:
Think of an Old Testament passage you have loved, and ask: where does it point to Christ?

When you feel your hopes are crushed, remember that the stranger on the road was alive.

Ask the Lord to open the Scriptures to you, so that your heart burns as you read.
prayerPrompts: Thank Jesus that he is alive, and walks with the discouraged.
Ask him to open your mind to understand the Scriptures.
Ask him to make your heart burn as you read.
